look_here_first: Find the rhizomatous PERENNIAL base, then inspect the lower stem leaves: oblong to lanceolate-oblong, 6–12 mm wide, with truncate to slightly heart-shaped bases. At fruiting check the pappus, a tiny thickened ring or erose crown <0.1 mm, NOT the conspicuous ~25 bristles of C. ericoides.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Master Pool Hays source, accepted identity reviewed 2026-10-10; Texas state-native per POWO but county native threshold unresolved.

morphology_keys.habit: Low, spreading or ascending perennial with rhizomes, not a distinct annual taproot; inspect the crown/rootstock.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate, flat herbaceous leaves, proximal cauline blades oblong to lanceolate-oblong, typically 6–12 mm wide; bases truncate to subcordate; leaves diminish distally.
morphology_keys.heads: Small solitary terminal radiate heads with pale rays and yellow disk florets; flowering color overlaps congeners.
morphology_keys.fruits: Pappus a minute thickened ring or erose crown under 0.1 mm (Flora of North America key).
best_field_traits: Examine basal and stem leaves including overlap and blade bases
Examine mature cypsela pappus with magnification

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. bellidifolia is a taprooted annual with non-overlapping flat leaves and a minute pappus ring; C. ericoides has very narrow densely overlapping leathery leaves and obvious pappus bristles in one series. C. parryi also rhizomatous but has narrower spatulate lower leaves 2–5 mm and a much larger hyaline crown 0.3–0.8 mm.
comparisons.cautions: Do not identify on pale ray florets, sprawling habit, or a single detached leaf; inspect mature pappus and perennial base.

diagnostic_image_needs: Rhizome and crown showing perennial base
Lower stem leaf with 6–12 mm width and base shape
Mature pappus ring at high magnification
